explanation: Metal was scarce, so for three years winners received plaster figures. After the war, the Academy swapped them for metal ones.

claims.text: Because of metal shortages, Oscar statuettes were made of painted plaster for three years during the Second World War.
After the war, winners could exchange their plaster statuettes for metal ones.
